seeds.description: (a) decode() raises KeyError when the input dict omits the CFSR address instead of defaulting to 0
(b) a missing HFSR address defaults to all-bits-set instead of 0
(a) raw is missing the AFSR entry, so it no longer has one entry per register
(b) raw["CFSR"] disagrees with the cfsr value decode() actually used to compute mmfsr/bfsr/ufsr (it stores only the MMFSR byte)
(c) raw["AFSR"] is pushed outside the unsigned 32-bit range unconditionally
(b) the raw dict's MMFAR and BFAR entries are swapped with each other, so raw disagrees with the values decode() actually used for mmfar and bfar
(a) the MMFAR entry in FaultStatus.raw is keyed by a misspelt name outside the six CMSIS register names instead of the literal string "MMFAR"
(b) FaultStatus.raw's key set drops the DFSR entry entirely, so it is not exactly the six CMSIS register names

(b) an extra seventh key ("SCB_CFSR", an alias alongside "CFSR") is present in FaultStatus.raw's key set, so it is not exactly the six CMSIS register names, even though all six original keys are still present
(a) HFSR constant does not match its documented Cortex-M SCB address
(b) FAULT_REGION_BASE is not equal to CFSR
(c) FAULT_REGION_SIZE is not 24 bytes (six words, CFSR through AFSR)
(a) a set bit (BFSR IMPRECISERR) is missing from the decoded output because its definition is dropped
(b) several set MMFSR bits collapse into fewer ActiveBit entries than are actually set
(c) an ActiveBit entry (FORCED) is present in faults even when its bit is not set
(d) the PRECISERR bit is reported under the wrong name (typo'd), not its canonical name from the reference table
(a) DFSR bits land in .faults instead of .debug
(b) an HFSR (CFSR-family) bit lands in .debug alongside the DFSR bits
(c) a set DFSR bit (EXTERNAL) is missing from .debug because its definition is dropped
(a) mmfar returns a numeric address even when MMARVALID (CFSR bit 7) is clear
(b) bfar is always None, so real evidence is lost even when BFARVALID (CFSR bit 15) is set
(c) MMARVALID and BFARVALID are swapped: MMARVALID now gates bfar and BFARVALID now gates mmfar
(a) afsr's bits are decoded into ActiveBit fault entries as if they had defined meanings
(b) afsr is gated by a validity check (CFSR BFARVALID) and becomes None, though no source defines such gating for AFSR
(a) STKOF is absent from the decoded output when set, because its entry is dropped from the UFSR bit table
(b) STKOF (UFSR relative bit 4 / CFSR absolute bit 20) is masked out and treated as a reserved/undefined bit before decoding
(a) any_fault is always True, so it reports True even with an empty .faults
(b) any_fault is always False, so it reports False despite a non-empty .faults
(c) any_fault is toggled by .debug: a breakpoint-only halt (DFSR set, no CFSR/HFSR) now reports any_fault True
(a) diagnosis is an empty string on a clean read instead of stating plainly that no fault is active
(b) diagnosis returns the same hardcoded placeholder text for every active-fault state instead of naming the active fault
(c) a known MMFAR/BFAR address is never appended to the diagnosis text even though the corresponding VALID flag is set
(d) a multi-bit active-fault state produces diagnosis text identical to one of its single-bit members' text, because only the first active fault is reported
(a) two bits from the same status byte (MMFSR) are reported with different category values
(b) two bits from different status bytes (MMFSR and BFSR) are reported with the same category value
(c) DEBUGEVT is categorized outside the HardFault family instead of sharing HFSR's category

decode() reads the six register words with dict.setdefault instead of dict.get, so calling it with a dict missing one or more of the six addresses silently inserts those keys (value 0) into the caller's own dict.

decode() memoizes the last FaultStatus in a module-level cache keyed only on the CFSR word ('if CFSR looks unchanged, nothing changed'), so a call can return a stale result computed from an earlier call's HFSR/DFSR/MMFAR/BFAR/AFSR whenever that earlier call happened to share the same CFSR value; this could incidentally also flip some FAULTS-N3/N4/N7 tests if those hold CFSR fixed while varying DFSR or the address registers across sequential calls in the same process, though a per-need isolated test run would see only FAULTS-N13's own before/after comparison go red.

refactors.description: Rename the local loop/extraction helper variable and inline the byte/halfword masks as named constants; pure renaming and constant-extraction, no register table, gating logic, category string, or output shape changes, so every clause (register addresses, bit tables, mmfar/bfar gating, any_fault, diagnosis, raw dict) is preserved exactly.

Replace the if/elif ternary-style gating for mmfar/bfar with an equivalent helper function call, and rewrite the any_fault property's bool(self.faults) as len(self.faults) > 0; both are value-preserving rewrites (same truth table, same None-vs-int outcome for every input), so FAULTS-N4 and FAULTS-N7 hold exactly as before, and nothing else in the module is touched.

needs_without_failing_test.violation: (a) AFSR's bits are decoded into ActiveBit fault entries in addition to being passed through as FaultStatus.afsr
needs_without_failing_test.why_unnoticed: test_faults_n5_a/b/c call make_words with nonzero afsr values but assert only on status.afsr, never inspecting status.faults/status.debug for extraneous entries; no other test in the suite combines a nonzero AFSR value with an assertion on the exact contents of .faults (the multi-bit checks such as test_faults_n2_c always use the default afsr=0). Confirmed empirically: extending decode() to also run _extract(afsr, ...) into faults left all 89 tests green.

needs_without_failing_test.violation: (b), instance 1: raw["CFSR"] holds mmfsr (the CFSR word masked to its low byte) instead of the full cfsr word
needs_without_failing_test.why_unnoticed: The only test comparing raw's per-register values to the words actually used, test_faults_n11_b_raw_values_match_the_registers_actually_used, picks a CFSR test value of 1 << 4 (MSTKERR), which lies inside the low byte, so mmfsr == cfsr for that specific input. test_faults_n11_a only checks the entry count; test_faults_n11_c uses CFSR=0; test_faults_n11_d sets CFSR to 0xFFFFFFFF, whose masked byte (0xFF) still satisfies the 32-bit-range assertion. Confirmed empirically: replacing "CFSR": cfsr with "CFSR": mmfsr in the raw= literal left all 89 tests green.

needs_without_failing_test.violation: (b), instance 2: raw["MMFAR"] and raw["BFAR"] are swapped with each other (each still carries a real register word, just the other one's)
needs_without_failing_test.why_unnoticed: Every test that checks raw's per-register values does so by set/multiset membership rather than by key: test_faults_n11_b compares sorted(status.raw.values()) against a sorted expected list, and test_faults_n11_c only checks `mmfar_word in status.raw.values()` / `bfar_word in status.raw.values()`. Both are satisfied by any permutation of the six values across the six keys; test_faults_n12_a/b check only the key set. No test does a keyed status.raw["MMFAR"] == mmfar_raw comparison anywhere. Confirmed empirically: swapping the two dict entries (leaving FaultStatus.mmfar/.bfar themselves correctly computed from the un-swapped local variables) left all 89 tests green.

behaviour_without_need.text: _diagnose() always places the MMFAR sentence before the BFAR sentence when both are present, and both before the VECTTBL/DEBUGEVT sentences, a fixed ordering the contract does not require.
_diagnose() never emits the literal FORCED meaning string from _HFSR_BITS; it substitutes either a ", escalated to a hard fault" suffix or a different standalone sentence.
_diagnose() never mentions the raw AFSR value anywhere in its text, even when FaultStatus.afsr/raw["AFSR"] is nonzero.
decode() reads words only through .get() and never mutates the caller's dict.
decode() silently ignores any key in words other than the six documented addresses; an unexpected extra key is neither reported nor rejected.
ActiveBit is declared frozen=True (immutable) while FaultStatus is a plain mutable dataclass.

Within each category, _extract() always yields entries in ascending bit-position order, and .faults is always assembled in MMFSR, then BFSR, then UFSR, then HFSR order, deterministic though the contract disclaims any required order.
FaultStatus.raw's keys always iterate in the fixed insertion order CFSR, HFSR, DFSR, MMFAR, BFAR, AFSR, though FAULTS-N11/N12 only require the key set.
